scope: Read-only production samples and isolated local profiling; no runtime optimization/deployment

fixture.model: Current migration YAML; synthetic fixture identities; not a byte-identical production clone

topology.local: Apple M5 Max, 18 logical CPUs, 36 GiB RAM; native Python 3.13 threaded Werkzeug, Jena 6.2.0/Java 25 probe, Xmx 8192 MiB
topology.production: VMware VM, 8 vCPUs presented as Xeon Gold 6226R; Gunicorn 4 workers/2 threads; no Docker CPU quota/cpuset on API/Jena; existing production service unchanged

dating_projection_control.scope: Local diagnostic projection only; dates remain required in the real UI

limits: Fresh browser contexts but warm backends; not a cold-start or capacity benchmark.
Local query timing uses current shared engine through probe timing headers, not the production wrapper. Java dispatch includes parse/evaluation/serialization; it is not pure SPARQL evaluation time.
Shares sum serial local API processing time across nine searches; they are not additive shares of browser critical-path time.
CPU profiling runs are separate and slower; latency tables use four unprofiled samples after warmup.
Older fixture has one fewer medium/person and different date payloads; class sizes match for all 437 objects/events.
No permission checks bypassed; dates omitted only for a local diagnostic control, not in the application.
DOM mutation readiness removes locator-polling overhead; final waterfalls use monotonic request events because one preliminary browser wall-clock timing was inconsistent.
No endpoint, validation, cache policy, production configuration or public function signature changed.
